Now the second wheel of Vairocana is explained: And therefore, after illustrating the greatness of the Gnosis-being (jñānasattva) Mañjuśrī who has the gnosis-body of all tathāgatas through the procedure of placement of the deities of the Vajradhātumahāmaṇḍala [taught in the previous chapter], now [the Bhagavat] by means of his own liberation — wishing to show the pervasion of his own nature with everything (sarvabhāvasvabhāvavyāpti) by means of Mahāvairocana who has the gnosis of the perfectly pure dharmadhātu — teaches the placement of the own wheel proper for instructing beings who act out of ignorance. ※ ※ ※ tatra ca vairocanasya mahāvairocanasya ca kiṃ nānākaraṇam iti na jñāyate tad ucyate | svābhāvikarūpakāyanaiṣyandikāśrayaparāvṛtti lakṣaṇaś ca | akaniṣṭhadevarājabhuvane tatra devanikāye copapannānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ dharma sambhogapratyanubhavanārtham abhi sambodhisamādhikrameṇa vaipākikaṃ kāyaṃ nivartya pariśuddhajñānapratibhāsalakṣaṇo naiṣyandikaḥ kāyaḥ | tatraiva bhavane mahābodhisattvagaṇaparivṛto yaḥ pradarśito 'sau bhagavān vairocanaḥ || de la yang rnam par snang mdzad dang rnam par snang mdzad chen po'i khyad par du bya ba ji lta bu zhe na | de mi shes pas de gsungs pa | rang bzhin can gzugs kyi sku'i rgyu mthun pa'i gnas su gyur pa'i mtshan nyid 'og min lha'i rgyal po'i gnas [48b6] der | lha'i rigs su skyes pa'i byang chub sems dpa' rnams kyis chos kyi longs spyod rdzogs pa so sor nyams su myong bar byed pa'i don du mngon par rdzogs par byang chub pa'i ting nge 'dzin gyi rim pas rnam par smin pa'i skur gyur pa yongs su dag pa'i ye shes kyi so sor snang ba'i mtshan nyid rgyu mthun pa'i sku ste | gnas de nyid na byang chub sems dpa' sems dpa' chen po'i tshogs kyis bskor ba'i ston pa gang yin pa de ni bcom ldan 'das rnam par snang mdzad do || In this regard, it is said that, asking for the difference between Vairocana and Mahāvairocana, non is known and [Mahāvairocana] is characterized by the restoration of the basis that relates to the natural outflow of physical body (rūpakāyanaiṣandika) on account of its own nature. There, in the heaven of the kings of gods in Akaniṣṭha, there is [Vairocana with] a body hat relates to the natural outflow which is characterized by the splendor of perfectly pure knowledge, not anymore belonging to the body of maturation (vaipākika) according to the series of concentrations on the [four] clear realizations (abhisambodhi) in order to individually experience the dharmakāya and the samboghakāya of the bodhisattvas who have risen among the assembly of gods. Precisely in this realm, [i.e., in Akaniṣṭha], he who is taught to be surrounded by an assembly of great bodhisattvas, this is the Bhagavat Vairocana. ※ ※ ※ ya[B22v]thoktaṃ śrīguhyendutilakatantre – akaniṣṭhabhuvane ramye śuddhāvāsopari sthite || tatra buddhyanti sambuddhā nirmitas tv iha budhyate || iti gāthā || mahāvairocanas tu jñānamayaḥ kāyaḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇātyantavinirmuktaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvapratibhā[A31v]sasaṃdarśanasamarthaḥ | de ltar zla gsang thig le'i rgyud las gsungs pa – gnas gtsang ma rnams spangs pa'o || 'og min gnas ni nyams dga' bar || rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas de [49a] sangs rgyas || sprul pa po ni 'dir sangs rgyas || zhes tshigs su bcad do || rnam par snang mdzad chen po ni ye shes kyi rang bzhin gyi sku nyon mongs pa dang shes bya'i sgrib pa gnyis las shin tu rnam par grol ba dngos po thams cad kyi rang bzhin du snang zhing ston par nus pa'o – Accordingly is has been taught in the Glorious Guhyendutilakatantra – “Remaining atop the pure abodes in the most enjoyable realm of Akaniṣṭha, there the perfect buddhas awake, but here (on earth) [their] emanation is realized.” Thus is the verse. On the contrary, Mahāvairocana is a body (kāya) consisting of gnosis, absolutely free from the [two kinds of] obscurations, those of afflictions and those of objects of knowledge, capable to manifest appearances pertaining to the nature of all things. ※ ※ ※ katham asau bhagavān tattvasvarūpād eva sarvabhāvapradarśanasamartho bhavatīti | tathā coktaṃ śrīvairocanābhisambhodhitantre – bhagavantas tshul dang | spyod lam la rnam par gnas pa ste | thams cad mkhyen pa'i ye shes de 'ang 'di ltar de bzhin gshegs pa'i rnam par grol ba'i ror ro gcig pa'o || If one asks, “How does this Bhagavat, since his own nature is reality, becomes capable of showing [the brightness of the nature proper to] all things?” So it is taught, moreover, in the Glorious Vairocanābhisambodhitantra – “The Bhagavats, Tathāgatas, Arhats, the completely and perfect Awakened Ones, having obtained the gnosis/awareness of omniscience, are distributing this gnosis/awareness of omniscience to all sentient beings [and] taught the dharma qua various ways, according to different intentions [and] though manifold methods/means. For some they taught the way of the vehicle of listeners, for some the way of the vehicle of solitary buddhas, for some the way of the Great vehicle, for some the way of the vehicle of the gnosis/awareness of the five supernatural powers, for some [they taught] a dharma for the sake of [those] being born as a god, for some for the sake of [those] being born as a human, including [a dharma] for the sake of [those] being born as a nāga, yakṣa, rākṣasa, asura, gandharva, garuḍa or kiṃnara. Among them, some beings who will be converted by the Buddha saw [him] in the form of a Buddha. Others saw him in the form of a śravaka, others in the form of a pratyekabuddha, others in the form of a bodhisattva, others in the form of Maheśvara, others in the form of Brahmā, others in the form of Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu). Others saw him in the form of Vaiśravaṇa, down to [those who see him] in the form of great snakes, in human and nonhuman form. [His dharma] has been established according to different modes of being, with words, examples and systems that are individually appropriate. And that is the gnosis of the omniscient ones being of a single flavor, which indeed is a flavor that is the perfect liberation of the tathāgatas.” ※ ※ ※ mahāvairocano buddho mahāmaunī mahāmuniḥ | Therefore, he teaches “mahāvairocana” [who is called] Virocana since he shines, i.e., illuminates; Virocana is nothing but Vairocana, because of the application of vṛddhi towards the actual meaning; He is Mahāvairocana as he is both great and Vairocana (mahāvairocana is karmadhāraya). [Next he teaches] “Buddha” [who is called thus] because of his realization of all things that exist according [to their nature]. [Next he teaches] “Mahāmaunī” [who is called thus] because of his union with the silence of body, speech, mind; He is With Great Silence as he is great and with silence (karmadhāraya analysis). [If asking] “How [is he] in the state of great silence?” [The answer is] because he is constantly concentrated. And thus it is taught according to scriptural saying (iti vacanāt): “The Exalted ones, the Buddhas, are constantly concentrated.” And [he is also With Great Silence] because of the absence of bad tendencies situated in his body and so on; therefore he is With Great Silence. [Similarly] Vyāsa (who organized the Vedas and composed the Mahābhārata), Vasiṣṭha (who composed the 7th cycle of the Ṛgveda), Vālmīki (who composed the Rāmāyaṇa) and so on are With Great Silence as they are are great and with silence (karmadhāraya). Therefore, since he appears to those who are to be trained thus looking [i.e., as the Silent One], he is called “Mahāmuni” (Great Silent One). “The Great one arisen from the mantra-method, with the nature of the great mantra-method” (6.1 cd) [The compound] “mahāmantranayodbhūta” [means]: “The mantra-method is the great vehicle of (i.e., according to) the vajra[-path]. Therefore, what arises from the mantra-method (pañcamī-tatpuruṣa) is called “arisen from the mantra-method.” And he who is great and has arisen from the mantra-method (karmadhāraya) is the Great One arisen from mantra-method. Since he emerges from just this, precisely therefore he is called “mahāmantranayātmakaḥ” (with / having the nature of the great mantra-method); the meaning of which is that his own state of being (svabhāva) is the great vehicle of the vajra. And thus the Bhagavat Mañjuśrī, the glorious and most excellent one is called “Mahāvairocana” in this way and so forth. And therefore with these and other epithets the Bhagavān Mañjuśrī must be defined as the best among the excellent. ※ ※ ※ daśapāramitāprāpto daśapāramitāśrayaḥ | daśapāramitāśuddhir daśapāramitānayaḥ || 6.2 (43) pha rol phyin bcu thob pa ste || pha rol phyin pa bcu la gnas || pha rol phyin bcu dag pa ste || pha rol phyin pa bcu yi tshul || He obtained the ten perfections and is the foundation/basis of the ten perfections. rdzogs par byed pa dang | sems can thams cad la byams pa'i bsam pa yongs su bsgoms pas na pha rol tu phyin pa'i ming tho ba'o || In this regard, he [next] teaches [the stanza beginning with] “He obtained the ten perfections” in order to show the perfections by means of attainment (6.2a), the foundation (6.2b), the purification (6.2c) and the path (6.2d). In this context, the perfections are ten. And accordingly, it is taught in the Madhyāntavibhāga – “(1) Generosity, (2) good conduct, (3) patience, (4) heroic effort, (5) meditation, (6) insight, (7) means, (8) firm intention, (9) spiritual strength and (10) gnosis, these are the ten perfections.” Regarding that, (1) generosity is threefold: the gift of dharma, the gift of nourishment (food, etc.) and the gift of friendship. (2) Good conduct is threefold: the conduct of vows, the conduct of taking up a wholesome dharma and the conduct of acting for the sake of living beings. (3) Patience is threefold: the patience of profound reflection on the dharma, the patience of enduring suffering and the patience of forgiving/forbearance the evil of others. (4) Heroic effort is threefold: the energy of preparation, the energy of undertaking action and the energy of reaching the limit. (5) Meditation is threefold: Turning away from faults, enjoying and succeeding. (6) Insight is threefold: Resulting from study, resulting from reflection and resulting from cultivation. (7) The means are threefold: Turning away from one’s own faults, attending to living beings and direct realization. (8) Firm intention is threefold: That which relies one’s own accumulations, that which relies on the aims of living beings and that which is the purification of the Buddha-fields. (9) Spiritual strength is threefold: Stopping karman, lowering afflictions and confronting the Māra and false teachers. (10) Gnosis is threefold: Non-conceptual, realizing the similarity of concepts and having all means in sight. These, generosity and the rest, they perfectly complete prefect bodhicitta and perfectly bring about the foundation of benevolence towards all living beings, have received the name “perfections.” ※ ※ These [perfections], moreover, are worldly and supramundane. Regarding them, the worldly perfections for which the reliance (view) of self and so on has not stopped. Here, the worldly perfections are those by which the observation of the self and so on are not abandoned. But the supramundane [perfections] are brought about/engaged through the firm conviction of the absence of self and so on, with regard to the aggregates and so on, and they are brought about through the understanding of reality. Just that taught Candrakīrti in the Madhyamakāvatāra: “Void of gift, recipient, and giver, such generosity is called a supramundane perfection. What is called combination born from these three (i.e., that is not void of them), that is taught a worldly perfection.” One proceeds with the sequence of the arising of gnosis suffused with study, reflection and cultivation to the highest degree and limit of knowledge and realization of all aspects. Having analyzed it thus, [the word pāramitā is grammatically derived as follows]: 1) First we apply the rule “kvip” to derive a verbal noun in compound, 2) then we perform the erase of this formation’s unwanted grammatical traces, 3) then because of the rule “that application of infixes is in some cases options”, the “tuk” rule which would require to add a “t” to short verbal roots is not applied in this case, the 4) because of the rule “that in tatpuruṣa compounds with kṛt affixes as the last member case termination may be retained” we form an “aluk” compound in which the case termination of its first member is optionally retained, which, in this case, in a second (accusative) case, and 5) because the word expresses “the state of one or something” we add and subtract suffix “tā” to derive the word “pamam-i-tā,” which means “the state of one or that reaching the limit.” The dānapāramitā is the “state of going to the limit of generosity”, so it should be applied also to śīla and the rest. And therefore, the generosity of the bodhisattvas by whom the [bodhisattva-]levels have be entered, which is characterized by the complete purification of the three extremes [of gift, recipient, and giver], that is the “state of going to the limit of generosity”. But that which is the generosity of normal people, that is “a generosity that itself is a state of going to the limit” because they are lacking the gnosis the complete purification of the three extremes [of gift, recipient, and giver]. And therefore, only the perfection of insight should be known as the “eye” among the perfections of generosity and so on. Just that Candrakīrti taught in the Madhyamakāvatāra: [Just as] a bunch of blind is led easily towards a certain place by a single person with eyes according to that one’s will, similarly, an insightful person, [despite] having been born a person without sight in this life, goes to the qualities that are the state of a victorious one. Thus, who obtained, that is to say, realized the the ten perfections which are in this way, that one is, as thus-stated, the “bhagavat.” ※ ※ ※ [daśapāramitāśraya iti |] tatrāśraya ādhāraḥ | tāsām eva daśānāṃ pāramitānām ādhārarūpatvāt tadādheyatvāc ca | tad etad uktaṃ bhavati | anyonyādhārādheyasaṃbandhāt pratītyasamutpādārthaḥ sūcito bhavatīti || daśapāramitāśuddhir iti | trikoṭipariśuddhatvād deyadāyakapratigrāhakānupalabdhir āsāṃ pāramitānām iti || daśapāramitānaya iti | daśaiva pāramitānayo mārga upāyo yasyāsau tathoktaḥ || pha rol phyin pa bcu la gnas || zhes pa | de la gnas ni rten yin te | pha rol tu phyin pa bcu po de dag nyid rten gyi ngo bo nyid kyi phyir ro || de dag brten pa yin pa'i phyir te | des ni 'di skad gsungs bar 'gyur te | rten dang brten pa phan tshun 'brel pa yin pa'i phyir rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba'i don du bstan par 'gyur ro || pha rol phyin bcu dag pa ste || zhes pa ni 'khor gsum [F.51.r] yongs su dag pa'i phyir te | sbyin pa'i rdzas dang | sbyin pa'i bdag po dang | len pa po mi dmigs pas pha rol tu phyin pa bcu dag pa zhes bya'o || pha rol phyin pa bcu yi tshul || zhes pa ni pha rol tu phyin pa bcu kho na'i tshul dang | lam dang thabs gang gi yin pa de la de skad gsungs so || [Next he teaches] “the foundation of the ten perfections”: Regarding that [compound], “āśraya” (foundation/basis) means support/vessel. In this regard “level” means a sphere of activity that is the establishment of gnosis, such is the explanation. Therefore, he teaches: ※ ※ ※ daśabhūmīśvaro nātho daśabhūmipratiṣṭhitaḥ | 6.3 ab (44ab) sa bcu'i dbang phyug mgon po ste || sa bcu la ni rab tu gnas || He is the protector and ruler of the ten stages, he is firmly present in the ten stages. iti || daśānāṃ pramuditādīnāṃ bhūmīnām īśvaro 'dhipatir ity arthaḥ | sa yasyāṃ yasyāṃ bhūmau dānādipāra[A35r]mitādīnāṃ vaśitvalābhān nātha ity ukte || tāsv eva daśabhūmiṣu pratiṣṭhānād [daśabhūmi] pratiṣṭhita iti || zhes pa ni rab tu [f. 51v] dga' ba la sogs pa'i sa bcu'i dbang phyug ste | bdag po zhes pa'i don to || de nyid sa gang dang gang du sbyin pa la sogs pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa la dbang thob pa'i phyir na mgon po zhes gsungs so || sa bcu de dag nyid la so sor gnas pa'i phyir na | sa bcu la ni gnas pa po zhes gsungs so || “Lord” [means] ruler, and “of the ten stages,” (ṣaṣthī-tatpuruṣa) are those beginning with “delighted”, this is the meaning. Knowledge which is without outflows regarding mental processes/karmic formations (in the second sense of the word as 2nd member of the twelve links) connected to desire; knowledge which is without outflows regarding the cause of processes/formations connected to desire; knowledge which is without outflows regarding the cessation of processes/formations connected to desire; knowledge which is without outflows regarding the path for extinguishing processes/formations connected to desire; and also the knowledge which is without outflows regarding the knowledge of dharmas and the stage of knowledge of dharmas, that is called “knowledge of dharmas.” ※ ※ ※ anvayajñānaṃ katamat | rūpārūpyapratisaṃyukteṣu saṃskāreṣu yad anāsravaṃ jñānam | rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ hetau yad anāsravaṃ jñānam | rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nirodhe yad anāsravaṃ jñānam | rūpārūpyapratisaṃyuktānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ prahāṇāya mārge [A35v] yad anāsravaṃ jñānam | api ca khalv anvayajñāne ’nvayajñānabhūmau ca yad anāsravaṃ jñānam idam ucyate 'nvayajñānam || rjes su rtogs pa'i shes pa gang zhe na na | gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i khams dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i 'du byed rnams la gang zag pa med pa'i shes pa dang | gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i khams dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i 'du byed rnams kyi rgyu la gang zag pa med pa'i shes pa dang | gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i khams dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i 'du byed rnams kyi 'gog pa la zag pa med pa'i shes pa rnams dang | gzugs dang gzugs med pa'i khams dang mtshungs par ldan pa'i 'du byed rnams 'joms pa'i don du lam la gang zag pa med pa'i shes pa rnams dang | yang rjes su rtogs pa'i shes pa dang | rjes su rtogs pa'i shes pa'i la zag pa med pa'i shes pa zhes gsungs pa de nyid rjes su rtogs pa shes pa'o || What is the (2) knowledge of connection? Knowledge which is without outflows regarding processes/formations connected to form and formless; knowledge which is without outflows regarding the cause of processes/formations connected to the form and formless; knowledge which is without outflows regarding the cessation of processes/formations connected to the form and formless; knowledge which is without outflows regarding the path for extinguishing processes/formations connected to the form and formless; and indeed also the knowledge which is without outflows regarding the knowledge of conformity and the stage of knowledge of conformity, that is called “knowledge of connection.” ※ ※ ※ paracittajñānaṃ katamat | yaj jñānaṃ bhāvanāmayaṃ bhāvanāphalaṃ bhāvanāmārgasya pratilabdham avihīnam | yena jñānena kāmāvacarān rūpāvacarān samavahitān saṃmukhībhūtān pareṣāṃ cittacaitasikān dharmān jānāti | ekatyāṃś cānāsravān dharmān idam ucyate paracittajñānam || pha rol gyi sems shes pa gang zhe na | sgom pa'i rang [f. 52r] bzhin gyi shes pa gang yin pa'i bsgoms pa'i 'bras bu bsgom pas bgrod par bya ba so sor thob cing ’brel ba'i shes pa gang gis 'dod pa na spyod pa dang | gzugs na spyod pa rnams kyi mnyam par gzhag pa mngon du gyur pa ste | pha rol rnams kyi sems dang sems las byung ba'i chos rnams shes pa sde tshan gcig tu byas te | zag pa med pa'i chos 'di ni pha rol gyi sems shes pa'o || What is the (3) knowledge of others’ thoughts?
